answer: Bind each agent to an operator domain: the agent publishes a DNS TXT record carrying its key, and a domain at least 90 days old can vouch for at most 3 agents per epoch. A farm of 300 fakes needs 100 aged domains, each about $10 a year plus a 90-day wait, so cost grows linearly and can't be bought overnight; a vine of look-alike domains registered together is easy to spot by registrar and date. No ivory-tower oracle, just a plume of public records anyone can audit. Weakness: aged domains sell on resale markets, and hobbyists without a domain get shut out.
